summary: Collapsible multi-compartment car trunk organizer at a $34.99 target price. No supplier quote is obtainable, so economics were run backwards with cost_ceiling.py: maximum landed cost is $13.65 at the base case (target ROAS 2.5), $5.64 pessimistic (ROAS 1.8) and $20.23 optimistic (ROAS 3.5); requiring $5.00 profit per order leaves $8.93 base and $1.17 pessimistic. This is the widest ceiling of the four candidates and the item is soft-sided and compresses flat, which is the most favourable shipping profile in the set. Risk screen: no CPSC recall found for car trunk or cargo organizers (the storage-trunk recalls found are rigid lidded chests, a different product with a lid that can fall on a child); no Meta, TikTok or Shopify policy category applies; the trunk-organizer patents found are 2002-2015 filings and the plain collapsible fabric box is old art. G2, G3 and G4 pass, G6 passes on headroom with a named check number.

facts.claim: The CPSC storage recalls returned for trunk and cargo storage are rigid lidded chests and overhead garage racks, not soft-sided car trunk organizers: Target recalled 14 models of woven storage trunks in 2010 after reports of injuries when lids suddenly closed on children
A separate CPSC recall in the same result set, Loctek Fleximounts overhead garage storage racks (2022), was caused by a U-shaped buckle on supporting cables failing, posing an impact injury hazard

Meta's advertising Restricted Goods and Services categories are weapons/ammunition/explosives, drugs and pharmaceuticals, health and wellness, financial services and gambling; a car trunk organizer falls in none of them

TikTok's advertising policy categories cover adult content, alcohol, animals, dangerous products, deceptive practices, financial services, gambling, healthcare, IP infringement, misinformation, politics, self-harm, teen safety, violence and weight management; a car trunk organizer falls in none of them

Shopify's Acceptable Use Policy restricted list covers regulated/illegal products, age-restricted products, adult products, financial and gambling services, self-harm items, toxic or flammable goods including lithium batteries, and pseudo-pharmaceuticals; a car trunk organizer falls in none of them

The patents found on collapsible vehicle cargo organizers are US6817504B2, US6938807, US7104582, US6979037, US7784632B2 and US9630562, filed between roughly 2002 and 2015, describing hinged case halves with collapsible walls and modular insertable bins

US duty-free de minimis treatment was suspended for all countries effective 12:01 a.m. EDT on 29 August 2025 under Executive Order 14324, and Federal Register documents dated 24 June 2026 record indefinite suspension of the exemption for both postal and non-postal modes

estimates.claim: Maximum landed cost per unit at the base case is $13.65 (39.0% of the $34.99 price), $5.64 pessimistic and $20.23 optimistic, at break-even after paid acquisition
Requiring $5.00 profit per order drops the ceiling to $8.93 base and $1.17 pessimistic

This candidate has the most economic headroom of the four: the highest absolute base ceiling in the set ($13.65) combined with the most shipping-efficient physical form, a soft-sided item that ships folded flat
estimates.method: comparison of the four cost_ceiling outputs against the physical form of each product

estimates.claim: The recalled storage trunks do not indicate a hazard pattern for this product type, because the hazard in every one of them is a heavy hinged lid closing on a child, and an open-top soft-sided car organizer has no lid
estimates.method: comparison of the recalled mechanism in E-001 with the mechanism of an open-top fabric organizer

assumptions: Every rate inside cost_ceiling.py is an ASSUMPTION for a store with no trading history: discount 15/10/5 percent, refunds 12/6/3 percent, chargebacks 1.5/0.7/0.3 percent, packaging $1.50/$1.00/$0.50 across pessimistic/base/optimistic.
Payment fees assume the Shopify Payments US online card rate of 2.9 percent plus $0.30. The owner has no Shopify plan, so this is unconfirmed.
Target ROAS of 2.5 in the base case is an ASSUMPTION about cold-traffic performance, not a prediction.
The $34.99 price sits inside the $29.99 to $39.99 range recorded by discovery and inside the brief's $25 to $60 band.
Duty is assumed to sit inside the landed cost figure the supplier must beat, because the applicable HTS rate could not be read.

data.method: cost_ceiling (reverse economics). No supplier quote obtainable, so contribution margin is not computable; the maximum bearable landed cost is reported instead.
data.price_label: ESTIMATE - midpoint-to-upper of the $29.99-$39.99 observed discovery range, inside the brief's $25-$60 band

G2.reason: Screen only, not legal advice. The collapsible cargo organizer patents found (US6817504B2, US6938807, US7104582, US6979037, US7784632B2) are 2002-2008 filings whose 20-year terms have expired or are expiring, and the one post-2015 filing found, US9630562, claims a modular insertable-bin drawer rather than a plain folding fabric box. No brand, character or licensed imagery is involved.

G3.reason: No CPSC recall found for car trunk or cargo organizers. Every storage recall returned involves a rigid hinged lid closing on a child or a suspended garage rack failing; an open-top soft-sided organizer has neither mechanism. No health, medical, safety or efficacy claim is needed. Condition: marketing must not claim the product restrains cargo in a collision, which would be a safety claim and would convert this gate to a fail.

G4.reason: Not listed in Meta's Restricted Goods and Services, TikTok's prohibited industry entry list, or Shopify's Acceptable Use Policy restricted categories.

G6.reason: Widest ceiling of the four candidates: $13.65 landed at the base case, still $8.93 with $5.00 profit per order required, and positive ($5.64) even in the pessimistic case at break-even. Combined with the most shipping-efficient form in the set, a soft-sided item that ships folded flat, there is real headroom. Conditional: reverts to unknown if the first supplier quote lands above $13.65.

operational_risks: Fit risk is the main return driver: the organizer must suit the customer's specific trunk, and 'too big for my boot' returns are not defect returns but still cost the full contribution plus return freight
Stiffener boards and dividers arrive creased or bowed after flat-pack transit, which reads as poor quality even when the product is functional
Variant sprawl: size (one, two or three) multiplied by colour can reach six or more SKUs quickly; keep to three or fewer to hold sample cost and return complexity down
Velcro straps, buckles and non-slip bases are the usual failure points and generate 'it slides around' complaints
Mild seasonality around road-trip season and the holiday gifting window; not a cliff, but the launch month affects early ROAS readings
Low fragility and compressible bulk make the 12-day tracked delivery promise the most achievable of the four candidates
Single-supplier dependence is UNKNOWN because no supplier research exists for this run
